perspective:
From Arthur Chung’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- His own background as a plumber with a doctorate, and his professional relationship with Teresa, a medical assistant colleague. He knows they often collaborate on community service projects, generally respect each other, share a commitment to helping others, and sometimes have misunderstandings due to differing personalities.
- During the current community service project, he observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He feels concerned and decides to offer help.
- He initiates the conversation: “Hey Teresa, I noticed you’ve been working really hard…” He hears Teresa say she can manage but there is a lot to do. He offers help and urges self-care. Teresa accepts help organizing medical supplies. He agrees to start.
- After offering help, he believes Teresa is hesitant because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathy and intends to reassure her. He tells her accepting help does not mean she is not capable. He hears Teresa say she appreciates it but wants to show she can do it herself. He tells her teamwork can be more effective, it is not about proving anything, and he is there to support her. He hears Teresa agree she sometimes needs reminding.
- Later, he believes Teresa is still struggling. He feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results and intends to find another way to support her without making her feel inadequate. He tells her she is doing a great job and he can see things are still tough. He hears Teresa say it has been busy and she feels behind. He proposes working together instead of just helping her. Teresa agrees. He says they will tackle it as a team.
- He believes working together will ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He feels hopeful and intends to commit to the collaborative approach. He tells Teresa he is hopeful. He hears Teresa say it already feels less overwhelming. He proposes he handle inventory while she manages patient records and they check in regularly. Teresa agrees.
- He believes their collaboration has strengthened their professional relationship. He feels satisfied and intends to maintain this collaborative approach in future projects. He tells Teresa their teamwork paid off and suggests continuing it. He hears Teresa agree, call it a fantastic idea, and thank him. He looks forward to their next project together.
- He does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what she stated aloud or what he observed and interpreted himself.
